popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: The Phrygian river beside which Priam's allies camp — Sangarius as the great stream of the Troad's hinterland, later named as Hecuba's divine father in genealogical tradition.

popCulture.title: Hecuba
popCulture.description: Priam's queen is often made a daughter of Sangarius — the river-god as the mythic father of Troy's most famous mourning mother.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus keeps Sangarius among the Oceanid rivers and in the Trojan stemma — the Phrygian stream that ties Hecuba to the earth's waters.

popCulture.title: Sangarius (mythology)
popCulture.description: Phrygian river-god, son of Oceanus and Tethys — the stream that gives its name to the Sakarya and, in many tellings, a father to Hecuba.
